newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaireans flock to airport to welcome Mobutu.
newsitem.headline: Zaireans flock to airport to welcome Mobutu.

text.p: Zaireans including dance and music groups gathered at Kinshasa airport on Tuesday to welcome their president Mobutu Sese Seko, who was due home after four months of cancer treatment and convalescence in Europe.
His homecoming has raised expectations in a country demoralised by the failure of the army to stop Rwandan-backed Tutsi rebels who have seized much of eastern Zaire.
Mobutu's jet took off from Nice airport at 8.50 a.m. (0750 GMT) for the seven-hour flight to Kinshasa.

Mobutu climbed aboard a special DC-8 plane bound for home after arriving at the airport with his entourage in three Mercedes cars, four minibuses and a taxi. Aides were seen loading items such as washing machines and televisions into one of the presidential planes.

Aides of Mobutu, who seized power in Zaire in 1965, say he is feeling better after surgery for prostate cancer in Switzerland in August. He has been staying at his private villa at Roquebrune-Cap-Martin near Nice since November 4.
A pro-Mobutu Zairean newspaper, The Soft, has said he planned to stay in Zaire just two or three weeks before returning to complete his convalescence.
But officials and presidential aides have declined to specify how long he will remain in Zaire.
It will be the first time that Mobutu has been to Zaire's capital since January this year when he visited the site of a plane crash that killed more than 300 people.
Since the beginning of a six-year political transition to democracy in 1990, he has preferred to remain in his jungle palace of Gbadolite in the northern Equateur Region.
State radio broadcast appeals on Monday to residents of Kinshasa to turn out in huge numbers for the 66-year-old Mobutu, who has ruled Zaire for 31 years.
A presidential press attache, Lumbana Kapasa, told reporters on Monday that Mobutu had interrupted his convalescence because the crisis in Zaire demanded his presence.
"Tomorrow he will be addressing the nation and he will say what is going to happen and why he has returned to Zaire despite his convalescence," Lumbana told a news briefing in the capital.

After welcoming ceremonies at Njili airport, Mobutu will cross the sprawling city to his fortified hilltop presidential residence in the Ngaliama district. He will address the nation in a televised speech from there at 5 p.m. (1600 GMT), Lumbana said.
Rwandan-backed ethnic Tutsis who took up arms in October ostensibly to defend their citizenship rights in Zaire, now say their objective is to overthrow Mobutu.

Local newspapers of all political tendencies speculated wildly on the implications of Mobutu's return and the possible changes in the government and the military that could follow. They were sharply divided on whether his presence would make any difference on the warfront.
